name_reason: Compliant with fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. 'enemy_turn_phase' accurately names the function (enemy AI turn phase entry point, called from fd2_run_full_turn_cycle Phase E). The 'team0' suffix is a domain ID (the team identifier; consts.h TEAM_ENEMY==0, matching the body's bTeam==0 filter), NOT a Ghidra address residue. It mirrors the sibling fd2_npc_turn_phase_team1 (team 1 = NPC allies), so the suffix is meaningful and consistent. Keep.
purpose: Enemy-team (team 0) AI turn-phase entry point: runs a two-pass loop dispatching each eligible enemy character's turn action, letting high-scoring casters act first.
logic_summary: Iterates runtime chars [0..party_member_count) twice. Eligibility filter (both passes): bTeam==0 (TEAM_ENEMY), (bFlags & 0x81)==0 (not dead 0x01 / not already-acted 0x80), sleep flag(+0x26)==0. Pass 1 (caster priority): for each eligible char score offensive spell + item, and dispatch the turn action only if best spell score >= 6 OR best item score >= 6; otherwise skip (char falls through to pass 2). Pass 2: dispatch unconditionally for each eligible char; chars that acted in pass 1 are excluded by the 0x80 acted bit set during pass 1. Both passes share an identical per-char postlude: clear keyboard buffer, set consequence index to 0xFF before acting, then if it is != 0xFF invoke data_fd2_battle_ai_post_action_consequence_table[idx], always call data_fd2_chapter_post_action_handler_table[current_chapter_id], and return early if data_fd2_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code != 0. Pass 1 also forces data_fd2_battle_anim_phase = 0 each iteration.

returns.semantics: No return value. Side effect is driving all enemy-team characters' turn actions for the current turn; loop terminates either when all chars are processed or when a chapter event / battle-end code is raised mid-loop.

comment_original_issue: Original source comment was correct but terse (two lines): it captured the two-pass caster-priority design but omitted the eligibility filter, the shared per-char postlude (consequence handler + per-chapter handler), and the mid-loop early-exit on the event/battle-end code -- functionally significant parts of each loop body and documented thoroughly on the sibling fd2_npc_turn_phase_team1.
notes: Single caller fd2_run_full_turn_cycle @0x1a30b (unconditional call from Phase E, the enemy turn, gated by event flag == 0; preceded by set enemy-turn BGM + load speed-mode overlay) -- confirms 'enemy-phase entry point per turn'. Decompile shows the source byte-offset arithmetic (pChar[6]/[5]/[0x26]) maps to the struct fields bTeam/bFlags/bStatus_sleep_flag; '> 5' in Ghidra == '>= 6' in src (integer-equivalent). Ghidra plate already fully consistent and detailed -> left untouched. No rename applied (Stage 2 handles renames); none needed anyway.
